ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of the circle $O$. The chord $CD \perp AB$ at point $E$, $OC = 5 \text{cm}$, $CD = 6 \text{cm}$, then what is the value of $BE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that AB is the diameter and CD$\perp$AB,\\
it follows that CE=$\frac{1}{2}$CD=$\frac{1}{2} \times 6=3$, and $\angle$OEC=$90^\circ$,\\
thus, OE=$\sqrt{OC^{2}-CE^{2}}=\sqrt{5^{2}-3^{2}}=4$,\\
which means BE=OB−OE=5−4=\boxed{1}cm.
